historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Pseudomonic-acid / isoleucyl-tRNA-synthetase inhibitors

starting.description: Investigators developed an antibacterial substance from the observed antagonistic activity of Pseudomonas fluorescens cultures: the inhibitory material was isolated and characterized as pseudomonic acid, the founding lead of the mupirocin family.

inspiration.description: Antibacterial antagonism observed in bacterial cultures led to isolation of the natural bacterial metabolite pseudomonic acid; the named 1887 observation is historical context, not proof that its active compound was identical.

steps.description: The Imperial College investigators isolated and characterized pseudomonic acid from the inhibitory products of P. fluorescens cultures, following evidence of antibacterial antagonism.
The inventors described an activity-guided isolation process: culturing a producer, removing inactive material, concentrating active fractions and separating pseudomonic acid from the mixture.
After pseudomonic acid had been isolated, investigators reported inhibition of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase, explaining a molecular target of the established natural antibiotic.

Systemic degradation limited oral and parenteral prospects, and Beecham researchers studied the established natural antibacterial agent for topical use, including tests against clinical skin isolates.

design.description: Researchers developed an activity-guided purification process and characterized the natural antibacterial material, then developed a topical application in response to systemic degradation; the cited testimony does not establish a new designed active chemical scaffold.

circumstances.description: The 1985 antibacterial evaluation for topical use was expressly designed for that purpose. The evidence does not establish whether the original observation or choice of strain was planned or unexpected.

limits: This record concerns the established pseudomonic-acid/mupirocin family represented by mupirocin, not every unrelated inhibitor of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase.
gaps: The full 1971 founding paper was not accessed; its publisher preview was read. The original strain-selection procedure and exact circumstances of discovery remain unestablished.
The 1980 target-mechanism original was read only as an abstract; the complete 1978 mechanism paper was not read. Neither limitation establishes how the original strain was chosen.
The identity of the person who proposed topical use and its precise priority are not established by the sources read.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Rapid loss of systemic activity in pharmacokinetic work helped direct mupirocin toward topical use.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Mixed human and animal experiments and analytical measurements; not a bedside discovery of antibiotic activity.
